class.name: SnowBodies3D
class.brief_description: Snow that moving things carry: rigid bodies, vehicles and cloth.
class.description: Keeps a snow load for every [RigidBody3D] (vehicles too), [AnimatableBody3D], PhysX vehicle and cloth, and any node in the [code]snow_catch[/code] group ([code]snow_ignore[/code] opts out). Falling snow builds the load where the sky is open above the body, at the new snow density; the ground's cover seeds it when a body is first seen; wind over the blowing threshold (Li and Pomeroy 1997, raised for wet and settled snow), counted as the air moving past the body, strips it; jolts over [member shake_threshold] throw it off; warm air, rain and fire melt and wet it. Weather, ground snow and fire are read through [WorldContracts]. A node in the [code]snow_roof[/code] group is a roof face: it keeps Eurocode's share of the snowfall ([method roof_shape]), holds up to [member roof_max_depth], and lets its load slide by [method slab_slides] with the friction of its roofing (meta [code]snow_roof_material[/code]: [code]metal[/code], [code]glass[/code], [code]tile[/code], [code]slate[/code], otherwise shingle, see [method roof_friction]). Meta [code]snow_roof_heat[/code] (W/m², heat lost through the roof) melts the bed under the load when it beats the snow's insulation, so a warm roof sheds sooner (Tobiasson 1988). What slides leaves the eave as rigid pieces ([member roof_slab_bodies]) that break when they hit hard and come to rest as snow in [SnowCover3D] where they stop, a dry one throwing up a puff of powder where PhysX Flow is present; with that off, it is thrown off the eave at the speed it slid down and lands as a bank of wind-packed snow ([member roof_piles]). On a heated roof in the cold, the bed's melt water freezes at the eave into an ice dam ([member ice_dams]) that holds the snow behind it while it stands a quarter of the snow's depth. The load reaches the body's materials through [member BaseMaterial3D.snow_on_body] (instance uniform [code]snow_body[/code], slot 12: depth in m, albedo, melt water, 1 + density / 1000), which the path tracer reads too. [SnowCover3D] adds one by itself while [member SnowCover3D.bodies_enabled].

method.name: get_body_density
method.description: The density of the body's snow, kg/m3 (0 if it is not tracked).

method.name: get_body_depth
method.description: The depth of snow the body carries, m (0 if it is not tracked).

method.name: get_body_load_mass
method.description: The mass of snow on the body, kg: depth times density times [method get_body_top_area]. Its weight presses on the top of a [RigidBody3D] every physics step while [member weight_enabled].

method.name: get_body_top_area
method.description: The body's footprint seen from above, m², from its meshes' bounds.

method.name: get_body_wetness
method.description: The melt water in the body's snow, 0 to 1.

method.name: get_clumps_dropped
method.description: How many clumps shed snow has made so far.

method.name: get_chunks_spawned
method.description: How many falling roof pieces have been made, breaks included.

method.name: get_falling_chunks
method.description: Roof pieces still falling or still on the roof waiting to leave the eave.

method.name: get_ice_dam_height
method.description: The height of the ice dam at a roof face's eave, m.

method.name: get_roof_landed
method.description: The mass of snow that has slid off roof faces and landed in the ground cover, kg.

method.name: get_roof_slides
method.description: How many times a roof face's load has slid off.

method.name: get_slabs_slid
method.description: How many loads have slid off as slabs so far.

method.name: get_tracked
method.description: The nodes that carry snow.

method.name: get_tracked_count
method.description: How many bodies carry snow.

method.name: is_carrier
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] for nodes tracked by themselves: rigid and animatable bodies, PhysX vehicles and cloth, and the [code]snow_catch[/code] group, not the [code]snow_ignore[/code] group.

method.name: is_tracked
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param node] carries a snow load.

method.name: set_body_depth
method.description: Sets the snow the body carries, m, and its density, kg/m³, when [param density] is given, tracking the body if it was not (a vehicle out of a garage, a scripted scene).

method.name: ice_dam_height
method.description: The height in m of an ice dam holding [param kg_per_m] of ice per metre of eave, drawn as a ridge twice as wide as high.

method.name: roof_friction
method.description: The dry bed friction angle in degrees for a roofing: 10 for [code]metal[/code] and [code]glass[/code], 20 for [code]tile[/code] and [code]slate[/code], 25 for anything else (shingles, boards, felt, thatch). Wetness lowers it by up to 10.

method.name: roof_shape
method.description: Eurocode 1 (EN 1991-1-3) roof shape coefficient mu1 for a pitch in radians: 0.8 up to 30 degrees, falling linearly to 0 at 60. A roof face gets this share of the ground's snowfall (relative to 0.8).

method.name: slab_slides
method.description: Mohr-Coulomb on the bed: [code]true[/code] when the load's shear, density times g times [param depth] times sin([param slope]) (radians), passes the bond [param cohesion] (Pa, lost with melt water) plus friction at [param friction] degrees (10 less when wet).

method.name: step
method.description: Runs one update of [param delta] seconds now (tests, scripted scenes).

method.name: track
method.description: Starts keeping a snow load for [param node], a [Node3D].

method.name: untrack
method.description: Stops keeping its load; its materials go back to their own snow.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the [BaseMaterial3D] materials of a tracked body get [member BaseMaterial3D.snow_on_body]; one that had no snow gets snow from the body only, so untracked instances sharing it stay bare.
If [code]true[/code], every node [method is_carrier] accepts is tracked as it enters the tree.
If [code]true[/code], snow that falls off a body (shaken, blown or sliding) lands on the snow as clumps ([method SnowClumps3D.drop]), as much as it holds together.
The most snow a body holds, m.

If [code]true[/code], melt water from a heated roof's bed freezes at the eave in the cold (all of it from -4 C; Tobiasson 1988) into an ice dam, drawn along the eave, that melts back in a thaw and holds the snow behind it.
The most snow a roof face holds, m ([member max_depth] is for other bodies).
If [code]true[/code], snow that slides off a roof face lands in the ground cover as a bank past the eave, its mass kept.

If [code]true[/code], a sliding roof slab leaves the eave row by row as irregular rigid pieces (about 1.2 m) that break in four on a hard landing and turn into snow in the cover where they come to rest, their mass kept, as a rounded heap ([method SnowCover3D.add_mound]) with the block sinking out of sight into it over 90 seconds. The pieces sit on collision layer 20 (with layer 1 in their mask), so ground height rays pass through them, and they carry the [code]world_contact_exclude[/code] meta, so they press no prints. If [code]false[/code], it lands at once as a bank ([member roof_piles]).
How fast jolts throw the snow off: the share lost per second per g over [member shake_threshold].
The acceleration that starts throwing snow off, in g.
The bond of dry snow to the surface under it, Pa; melt water takes it away (see [method slab_slides]).
If [code]true[/code], the load on a tilted top slides off as one slab when [method slab_slides] says so.
If [code]true[/code], the load's weight presses on the top of each [RigidBody3D] that is not frozen.
How fast wind over the blowing threshold strips the snow: the share lost per second per m/s over it.
